Referring back to the subject, or having an object equal to the subject.
Of a relation R on a set S, such that xRx for all members x of S (that is, the relation holds between any element of the set and itself).

examples.text: "Equals" is a reflexive relation, as it holds for all possible x; "not less" is non-reflexive because it is true only for some x and y, "unequal" is irreflexive, as it never holds between x and itself.

glosses: Of or resulting from a reflex.

examples.text: The electric shock elicited an automatic and reflexive response from him.

glosses: Producing immediate response, spontaneous.

examples.text: a reflexive dislike

glosses: Producing or provoking a reciprocal response.

examples.text: Shoigu's thinly veiled nuclear threats against NATO are part of the Kremlin's broader reflexive control campaign to influence Western decision-making in Russia's favor and against Western states' own interests. Shoigu's nuclear threats are attempts to push European states to self-deter and reduce their buildups of their defenses – leaving NATO's eastern border largely undefended. These reflexive control efforts are in line with Russian President Vladimir Putin's 2021 demand before launching his full-scale invasion of Ukraine that NATO not deploy any military forces to states that became NATO members after 1997, including Poland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland.

glosses: Synonym of reflective.
A reflexive pronoun.
A reflexive verb.
An automatic response to a simple stimulus which does not require mental processing.

examples.text: For a while, I shall have to make a conscious effort to smile, nod, stand and perform the thousands of little gestures which constitute life on Earth, and then those gestures will become reflexes again.

He met Luis Suarez's cross at the far post, only for Chelsea keeper Petr Cech to show brilliant reflexes to deflect his header on to the bar. Carroll turned away to lead Liverpool's insistent protests that the ball had crossed the line but referee Phil Dowd and assistant referee Andrew Garratt waved play on, with even a succession of replays proving inconclusive.

glosses: The descendant of an earlier language element, such as a word or phoneme, in a daughter language.

glosses: The descendant of anything from an earlier time, such as a cultural myth.

examples.text: The superstition of the loup-garou, or werewolf, belongs to the folklore of most modern nations, and has its reflex in the story of "Little Red Riding-hood" and others.

glosses: A reflection or an image produced by a reflection; the light reflected from an illuminated surface to one in shade.

examples.text: A reflex camera uses a mirror to reflect the image onto a ground-glass viewfinder.

glosses: Produced automatically by a stimulus.

examples.text: It's easier to focus on the particular relationship or object (as in 'pornography', for example) than on the sexist (racist, ageist, etc.) attitudes that generate the almost reflex violence taught in our schools, churches, legal processes, families, mass entertainment, and advertising propaganda.

glosses: Having greater than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees.

examples.text: P denotes a polygon and r the number of reflex vertices.
A polygon is said to be convex when no one of its angles is reflex.

An angle less than a right angle is said to be acute; one greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle is said to be obtuse; one greater than a straight angle but less than a perigon is said to be reflex or convex.
If the reflex region is the interior of the angle, the dihedral angle is reflex.
A reflex edge of a polyhedron is an edge where the inner dihedral angle subtended by two incident faces is greater than 180°.
We say that an angle is convex if it is not reflex.
